people.about:
In 2002, after finishing her PhD at the UAB, she moved as a Marie Curie Fellow to the Leibniz Universität Hannover (Germany) and from 2005 to 2010, she was ICREA researcher. From 2010 to 2023, she was associate professor at the UAB.

In the last years, she has worked in the control of the external degrees of freedom of matter waves and in the use of ultracold atoms in optical lattices as quantum simulators. She has 80 peer-reviewed publications with more than 3900 citations (31/1/2025) and is co-author with Prof. M. Lewenstein and Prof. A. Sanpera of the book Ultracold atoms in optical lattices: simulating quantum many body physics, Oxford University Press 2012.

V.A. has supervised 8 PhD Thesis (presently supervising 2 more), 9 Master Thesis and 33 final degree works (3 more under elaboration). She has been awarded with the PhD extraordinary award and the excellence research award of the UAB.

From January 2011 to April 2014, V. A. was academic coordinator of the Physics degree and of the double degrees of Physics-Mathematics and Physics-Chemistry of the UAB and from June 2014 to September 2016, she was vice-dean of the Science Faculty of the same university. From July 2016 to July 2018, she was scientific collaborator of the Agencia Estatal de Investigación. Since January 2021 she is academic coordinator at the UAB of the Interuniversity Photonics master and the Europhotonics master.

Dr. Juan Campos has worked in optical image system quality, optical pattern recognition, diffractive optics, and metrology. His contributions to the field include: the design of non-uniform pupils in optical systems to modify different parameters of the image quality; the application of apodizers in photolithography; modeling, characterization and use of liquid crystal spatial light modulators; introduction of color information in optical pattern recognition; numerical methods to obtain the surface profile from deflectometry data; numerical methods to handle redundant information in interferometric measures to obtaine higher accuracy; use of liquid crystals to build Stokes and Mueller polarimeters.He has published more than 270 papers in scientific journals, 3 book chapters and presented more than 250 communications to National and International conferences, 13 of them invited papers.

Prof. Juan Campos has been the supervisor or co-supervisor of 18 Ph.D. Thesis, and supervisor of 19 Master Thesis. He is Fellow member of the OSA, SPIE, and EOS

people.about:
I am a theoretical physicist with an international and multidisciplinary research career at the interface between high-energy, atomic, and condensed matter physics. My activity is focused on quantum simulation of many-body physics in atomic systems. My goal is to propose viable experimental schemes to emulate high-energy and condensed matter phenomena (quantum magnetism, topological order, abelian and non-abelian gauge theories, Unruh effect). I have also worked on critical phenomena, stochastic processes, supergravity, and string theory.

Current research: Since 2009 I work on quantum simulation, first as Postdoc at the University of Barcelona (UB) with J. I. Latorre (2009-10), then as Research Fellow at ICFO with M. Lewenstein (2011-17), and finally as Senior Postdoc at IQOQI/University of Innsbruck (UIBK) with P. Zoller (2018). I joined UAB in 2019 and built an independent research line on quantum simulation of gauge theories with Rydberg atoms and Raman-dressed gases, before as a UAB-Talent Researcher (tenure-track position), and since 2023 as Professor Agregat (Associate Professor) and Visiting Professor at ICFO. My research activity is internationally recognized and has led to several high-impact publications (Nature, Nature Photonics, Phys. Rev. X, PRX Quantum, Phys. Rev. Lett., Quantum), invited talks in major conferences (DAMOP), supported by national and international projects.

people.about:
Dr. Irene Estévez obtained her PhD degree in Physics at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (Spain) in December 2018. Her PhD thesis was awarded with the PhD Extraordinary Award. She has been a visiting research scholar at the École Polytechnique (France) for four months in 2016. From 2019 to 2022, she was a postdoctoral researcher at the Physics Center of Minho and Porto Universities (CFUMP) (Portugal). Her postdoctoral research was marked within a collaboration between the CFUMP and the international company BOSCH in the framework of a European project. In 2023, Dr. Estévez was a Beatriu de Pinós postdoctoral fellow at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona.

Irene Estévez’s research interests include polarimetry (measurement and interpretation of polarized light), optical design and polarized light applications.

She has published fifteen peer-reviewed articles in high-impact journals in the field of optics and multidisciplinary sciences. In addition, she has three patents, two of them transferred to BOSCH. Dr. Irene Estévez has also presented some of her research at the most prestigious national and international conferences in the field. She is co-supervisor of 3 Ph.D. Thesis.

Dr. Irene Estévez is member of the SPIE, Optica (formerly OSA) and Sociedad Española de Óptica (SEDOPTICA).

people.about:
Dr. Angel Lizana completed his MSc degree in Physics and PhD in Physics at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (Spain) in 2006 and 2011, respectively. His research interests include liquid crystal displays and their application to diffractive optics, as well as the design and implementation of polarimeters. He is also interested in the study of polarimetric methods for the enhanced visualization and classification of biological tissues of both animal and vegetal origin.

He has been a postdoctoral scientist in the Laboratoire de Physique des Interfaces et des Couches Minces (LPICM) of the École Polytechnique (France), in 2011-12 and in 2013-2014, where he has worked in the optimization and implementation of a polarimeter able to operate in the infrared spectrum, and in the analysis of polarimetric information for its application to the characterization of samples.

He has published more than 70 papers in scientific journals, 2 book chapters and presented more than 80 communications to National and International conferences. He has been co-supervisor of 4 Ph.D. Thesis.

Dr. Angel Lizana is member of the SPIE and of Sociedad Española de Óptica (SEDOPTICA). From 2019 to 2023, he was secretary general of SEDOPTICA

people.about:
Dr. Jordi Mompart received his PhD in Physics from the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB) in 1999 with the Thesis entitled “Lasing without inversion” and under the supervision of Prof. Ramón Corbalán.

Dr. Jordi Mompart has been a visiting researcher at several universities and research institutes worldwide: Universität Münster, Università degli Studi Milano, Texas A&M University, Leibnitz Universität Hannover, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, and Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology. After a postdoctoral stay at the Leibniz Universität Hannover, where he worked on the use of cold atoms for quantum information purposes, he became associate professor at the UAB. His research interests range from laser physics and quantum optics to quantum information and artificial intelligence.

He is author of more than 100 articles, co-editor of the book “Applied Bohmian mechanics: from nanoscale systems to cosmology”, Pan Stanford Publishing 2012 and 2019, and holds three patents. He has supervised 8 PhD thesis. Presently, he is the coordinator of the Physics Doctorate program at the UAB.

people.about: Dr. Axel pérez-Obiol was trained as a nuclear physicist at Universitat de Barcelona with a PhD in effective field theories for weak nuclear interactions (2014) under the supervision of Assumpta Parreño and Bruno Juliá. He then spent almost seven years abroad as a postdoc researching in condensed matter and mathematical physics, first in the Nuclear Physics Institute in Prague (2014-2017) and then in Kochi University of Technology (2017-2020) in Japan. From 2021 to 2024 Axel worked at the Barcelona supercomputing Center devising and testing quantum algorithms for condensed matter physics. Since February 2024 Axel enjoys a Lecturer position at Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona. His current research at UAB focuses on ultracold gases, in particular atomtronics, and on simulating condensed matter systems and atomic nuclei with digital quantum computers.

people.about:
Adam Vallés received his BSc in telecom engineering from the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) in 2011, his MSc in photonics from the Institut de Ciències Fotòniques (ICFO) in 2012, and his PhD in photonics also from ICFO in 2017, where he had the opportunity of designing and implementing quantum optics-based experiments. He was then awarded a Claude Leon Foundation postdoctoral fellowship to work in the Structured Light Lab from the University of the Witwatersrand, South Africa. He also worked as Assistant Professor at Chiba University, Japan, devising novel imaging techniques for the terahertz region.

After over 4 years of postdoctoral experience supervising students and leading international projects in collaboration with Heriot-Watt, Naples, Tohoku or Harvard universities, among others, he joined the Optoelectronics group in ICFO where he is currently working as a Research Fellow. He is also lecturing in different BSc courses in Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB) and in the Photonics MSc coordinated by UPC, UAB, ICFO and also Universitat de Barcelona (UB). His research interests are mainly focused on high-dimensional quantum communication and quantum imaging.

people.about:
Dr. Gaspar Orriols has done experimental and theoretical research on Laser Spectroscopy and Quantum Optics, Nonlinear Optics and Nonlinear Dynamics since 1975, first at the Istituto di Fisica Atomica e Molecolare del CNR (Pisa) and then at the Physics Department of the UAB. His main findings include (the participation in) the discovery and explanation of the energy pooling phenomenon in collisions between excited atoms and of the coherent population trapping, which has now become a classical issue in quantum optics. He built up a research group at the UAB devoted to Nonlinear Systems with findings on optical bistability (cavity optimization by separating functions in thermo-optical bistability), nonlinear dynamics (amplitude death effect in coupled oscillators and full instability behavior in the Generalized Landau scenario), nonlinear optics (second harmonic generation in poled glasses) and multilayer optics (patent on a technique for best visualization of blood vessels).

His current research goals include the analysis of potential connections of the Generalized Landau scenario with the complex oscillatory behaviors of fluid turbulence and brain dynamics, as well as with the structural evolution of systems at both macro and microscopic scales.

people.about:
Dr. María J. Yzuel was a Full Professor of Optics at this Department from 1983 to 2011. Formerly she was a Professor of Optics at the Universities of Zaragoza and Granada, Spain. She is a member of the Royal Academy of Sciences and Arts of Barcelona, and a Correspondent member of the Academies of Sciences of Granada and Zaragoza, both in Spain. She earned her Physics degree and Ph. D. Degree from the University of Zaragoza, Spain. She was a postdoctoral visitor (1967-1968) at the University of Reading, UK, with a scholarship from the British Council.

She has worked in diffraction image theory, image quality evaluation, apodization, applications to photolithography, optical pattern recognition, color information in correlators, design of filters. She also worked in medical optics and in liquid crystal panels applied in diffractive optics. She has published more than 250 papers, and she has supervised 20 Ph. D. Thesis.

She is a Fellow member of the SPIE (The International Society for Optics and Photonics), the Institute of Physics (IOP), the OSA (Optical Society of America), the EOS (European Optical Society), and Socia de Honor of the Spanish Optical Society (SEDOPTICA) and the Spanish Royal Physics Society (RSEF). She served as President of SEDOPTICA from 1993 to 1996. She was Vice President of the Spanish Royal Physics Society. She was Vice President of the International Commission for Optics from 1990 to 1996 and from 2011 to 2017. She served in the SPIE Board of Directors from 2001 to 2003 and from 2007 to 2011. She has served in several SPIE and OSA (now OPTICA) Committees. She was the SPIE 2009 President. She was a member of the Board of Directors of COSCE (Confederación de Sociedades Científicas Españolas) (2015-2019).

In 2005 she received the SPIE Board of Directors Award and the Medal of the University of Warsaw. She received the Award of Commander of the Civil Order of King Alfonso X the Wise from the Ministry of Education in 2013. She has received other awards, among them the Medal of Physics given by the Spanish Royal Physics Society and the BBVA Foundation in 2014, the Gender Equality Award (Premi igUAltat) of the University of Alicante in 2017, and the SPIE President Award in 2021. She became Doctor Honoris Causa from the University Miguel Hernandez of Elche in 2012 and Doctor Honoris Causa from the University of Granada in 2017.

In 2015 she was the President of the Spanish Committee for the International Year of Light and Light-based Technologies. Since 2017 she is the President of the Spanish Committee for the International Day of Light.

people.about: I am a postdoctoral researcher at UAB, Bellaterra (Barcelona), working in the theory group led by Alessio Celi and in close collaboration with the ultracold quantum gases group at ICFO, led by Leticia Tarruell. Here I mainly work on resource efficient reformulations of two-dimensional non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, with the purpose of proposing feasible digital and/or analog quantum simulation schemes for such theories. My other current research projects regard topological properties of three-dimensional materials, higher-order topological phases of matter and two-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard models.

people.about:
Javier earned his BSc in Physics from the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM). He then pursued a double master’s degree in Photonics at Aix-Marseille University (AMU) and the Polytechnic University of Catalonia (UPC). For his MSc thesis, conducted at the Institute of Photonic Sciences (ICFO), he designed and built a high-dimensional entangled photon source based on orbital angular momentum, which he used for characterizing custom-made few-mode optical fibres.

He joined the group in November 2024, and his main research interests include high-dimensional quantum communications, entanglement distribution, and nonlinear quantum sensing.

people.about: Marc Miranda is pursuing a PhD under the supervision of Prof. Alessio Celi. Our goal is to advance schemes for the quantum simulation of topological and gauge theories in ultracold atom systems. In particular, the main objective of the project is the simulation of a quantum spin liquid, a phase of matter with very exotic properties: anyonic and fractionalized excitations, topological degeneracy and long-range quantum entanglement.

people.summary: Fengtao Pang is a joint Ph.D. student working with Prof. Alessio Celi. He comes from the Ultracold Atom Research Group at Shanghai University, where he is supervised by Prof. Yongping Zhang.
people.about:
Fengtao Pang is a joint Ph.D. student working with Prof. Alessio Celi. He comes from the Ultracold Atom Research Group at Shanghai University, where he is supervised by Prof. Yongping Zhang.

His research focuses on the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) excitations and dynamics of spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates (SOC-BEC). Specifically, he specializes in applying hydrodynamic approaches to study BECs subject to synthetic magnetic fields, and explores BdG excitations within the effective mixture model of the stripe phase.

people.about:
Dr. Octavi López started research in 1996 in the Optics Group of the Physics Department of the UAB and since then he has specialized in the characterization of spatial light modulators and their applications in diffractive optics. In 2007, he obtained his doctorate in physics at the UAB with the thesis «Control of the response of an optical system by means of non-uniform transmission pupils and multiplexed lenses». He has been an adjunct professor in the Optics and Optometry studies at the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) and has been adjunct professor in the Department of Physics at the UAB since 2000.

He combines teaching and research in optics with professional work in the field of scientific communication at the Communication Unit of the rectorate of the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona.

people.about:
Pep Vidal

Rubí, Barcelona, ​​1980.

Graduate in Mathematics and PhD in Physics. I work with infinitesimal changes, changes that always occur, everywhere. Imperceptible changes, chains of changes, changes forever… most of them, we neither see nor are aware of them. That’s my workspace.

I combine my artistic practice with that of being a professor of “Optics Laboratory”, in the degree of Physics, at the Autonomous University of Barcelona.

I have shown my work in more than 50 exhibitions, nationally and internationally, among which I would highlight Abrons Arts Center (New York), Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya MNAC (Barcelona), Kunsthaus Baselland (Basel), ISELP Contemporary art center (Brussels), Fundació Joan Miró (Barcelona), CAPC musée d’art contemporain de Bordeaux (Bordeaux), CaixaForum (Barcelona) or Fundació Antoni Tàpies (Barcelona). I have done some residencies, among which I would highlight Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten, Amsterdam, 2018.

I am represented by: ADN Galería, in Barcelona, ​​and LMNO, in Brussels.
